newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dollar ends slightly up vs mark, down vs yen in HK.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends slightly up vs mark, down vs yen in HK.

text.p: The dollar closed marginally higher against the mark compared with New York's Thursday close but was off its Asian highs on speculative selling triggered by better-than-expected German trade figures.
* "Participants used the better-than-expected German current account deficit and trade surplus released in late afternoon as an excuse to sell dollar/mark," a local bank dealer said.
* Germany's October trade surplus rose to 11.1 billion marks from 8.3 billion marks a month earlier while the current account deficit eased to 1.3 billion marks from 1.6 billion marks.
* But dealers said they expected the German figures to merely create chances for traders to buy the dollar on dips as bullish dollar sentiment remained intact.
* The dollar was slightly easier against the yen after a day of range-bound trading.
* "Dollar/yen eased further this afternoon on market rumours that the Bank of Japan would come out to talk up the yen after the holiday," a U.S. bank dealer said.

* Dealers in Singapore said the dollar was undergoing a correction after its recent sharp rise, but it was likely to remain well contained within the range of 114-116 yen and 1.5400-1.5600 marks for the time being.
* "I believe we'll be stuck in a range for a while. I don't expect the market to fly off immediately when Tokyo returns as it did last year," a European bank dealer said in Singapore.

* He also said sterling had returned to its pre-end 1996 levels. "I think people took the New Year as a chance to push it up. I think it will be well bought until the British elections. I'm looking for it to reach $1.72," he said.
* A more cautious Hong Kong trader said he preferred to wait until next week when the market returned to full swing to decide on the dollar's immediate trend.
* "I basically agree that the dollar's correction has been basically completed and is nurturing a new round of rallies," he said.
